item.title: Oct W2 26 - 01: The Effectiveness of Cognitive, Kinesthetic, Visual- Auditory and Technology-Based Approaches in Polyrhythm Teaching: A Systematic Synthesis (Tuğba ÇAĞLAK EKER)
item.description:
The Effectiveness of Cognitive, Kinesthetic, Visual- Auditory and Technology-Based Approaches in Polyrhythm Teaching: A Systematic Synthesis - Tuğba ÇAĞLAK EKER - 2026 https://doi.org/10.46328/ijtes.8646
International Journal of Technology in Education and Science (2026). The purpose of this study is to synthesize the effects of polyrhythm teaching techniques based on different approaches developed as alternatives to traditional counting techniques by reviewing studies in the relevant literature. 5 publications that comply with the criteria identified within the scope of the research were examined in detail, and the pedagogical techniques, methodological approaches, assessment and measurement tools used in these studies, and the findings are comprehensively analyzed thematically. The synthesis of the studies examined reveals that the determining factor in polyrhythm learning is not the superiority of a single method, but rather the complementary functional roles of different approaches. Cognitive and verbal approaches form the basis for the mental analysis of complex rhythmic structures and the achievement of conceptual clarity; while technology-based approaches accelerate the process of transforming these mental schemas into physical performance through action observation and immediate feedback mechanisms. Modeling and motor skill-focused approaches ensure that the learned rhythmic structure reaches musical maturity and that the performance quality becomes permanent. Consequently, a holistic approach wherein logical grasp, technological mediation, and motor training converge offers a robust framework for enhancing the overall quality of polyrhythm performance.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 02: Musical Episodic Modulation of Human Functioning: Anticipation Mechanisms, Personal Sense, and Emotional Recall (Rodrigo Drumond Vieira)
item.description:
Musical Episodic Modulation of Human Functioning: Anticipation Mechanisms, Personal Sense, and Emotional Recall - Rodrigo Drumond Vieira - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1007/s12124-026-10033-0
Integrative Psychological and Behavioral Science (2026). This article develops a theoretical and exploratory account of musical episodic modulation of human functioning, with special attention to emotional recall. It responds to a recurrent limitation in the psychology of music: although music's effects on attention, emotion, memory, motivation, and performance have been widely documented, these domains are often examined separately rather than as mutually organized dimensions of lived episodes. The article proposes that music may function as a modulating agent of human functioning when its temporal, affective, and semantically open structure becomes coupled with ongoing activity through anticipation mechanisms. Drawing on activity theory, phenomenology of temporal consciousness, floating intentionality, entrainment, and appraisal theory, the paper conceptualizes anticipation mechanisms as the dynamic relations among anticipators, the anticipated, and horizonality. These mechanisms explain how musical signals may organize salience, attention, affect, readiness, and possible next actions over time. The argument is illustrated through a phenomenologically oriented self-study in which the same song contributed to opposed emotional episodes during two recall activities: hopelessness, yearning, and sadness in relation to the memory of a deceased father, and excitement, hope, and joy in relation to an anticipated romantic encounter. The contrast suggests that musical valence does not determine emotional outcome by itself. Rather, emotions emerge through projection-appraisal loops involving objects of thought, personal sense, belief systems, previous experience, and the unfolding music. The article concludes by outlining limitations, future research directions, and distinguishing the more specific phenomenon analyzed from the broader account of musical modulation of human functioning.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 03: The role of socio-cognitive abilities in adolescent and young adult romantic relationships: a systematic review (Nikica Polak et al.)
item.description:
The role of socio-cognitive abilities in adolescent and young adult romantic relationships: a systematic review - Nikica Polak et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1007/s12144-026-10100-0
Current Psychology (2026). Abstract High-quality romantic relationships are linked to better psychological well-being, yet adolescents and young adults vary in the quality of their romantic experiences. Socio-cognitive abilities, including empathy, emotion regulation, and theory of mind, may play a role in shaping romantic outcomes. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from 26 studies to examine how these abilities relate to romantic relationship quality in adolescents and young adults, following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Given the limited research on theory of mind in this population, perspective-taking was additionally included as a closely related socio-cognitive process. Findings indicate that the relational value of these abilities depends substantially on which subcomponent is engaged: empathic concern and cognitive reappraisal were consistently associated with higher relationship satisfaction and more constructive conflict resolution, while personal distress and expressive suppression showed the opposite pattern. Perspective-taking also showed consistent positive associations. Research on theory of mind in romantic contexts remains scarce, but available evidence suggests a promising role in partner well-being and emotion regulation. The review further identifies an asymmetry between actor and partner effects and addresses developmental and gender-related patterns. Overall, the review highlights the possible interdependence of socio-cognitive abilities in adolescent and young adult romantic relationships and the limited evidence available on theory of mind.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 04: Sensory Processing and Executive Functioning Interaction in Neurodevelopmental Disorders and At-Risk Conditions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis (Stefano Scatigna et al.)
item.description:
Sensory Processing and Executive Functioning Interaction in Neurodevelopmental Disorders and At-Risk Conditions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis - Stefano Scatigna et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neubiorev.2026.107010
Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews (2026). This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the relationship between sensory processing (SP) and executive functioning (EF) in children and adolescents (ages 0-18) diagnosed with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) or at-risk conditions, such as prematurity and genetic syndromes. Adhering to PRISMA guidelines, the results of 30 peer-reviewed studies were analyzed by qualitative and quantitative analyses to evaluate the strength and nature of these associations. The findings revealed a consistent and significant correlation between SP and EF, with effect sizes (r) ranging from r =.19 to r =.77. Meta-analytic synthesis confirmed a medium effect size (d =.58). While substantial heterogeneity was observed (I^2 = 82.9%), it was not moderated by the specific diagnosis of NDDs, age, EF component or correlation adjustment status. Notably, assessment modality served as a significant moderator: performance-based measures demonstrated higher associative strength and lower heterogeneity compared to questionnaire-based or combined assessment. Regression models indicated that SP measures statistically accounted for a substantial portion of EF variance (28-71%), while comparative analyses showed moderate-to-large differences in EF performance (η² =.10-.34) between typical and atypical sensory profiles. Furthermore, mediation analyses suggested significant indirect associations involving EF, particularly emotion regulation and inhibitory control, in the relationship between sensory processing and adaptive and functional outcomes. The evidence underscores a robust interdependence between sensory processing and executive functions in clinical and at-risk pediatric populations. These findings highlight the potential relevance of considering both sensory and executive domains in assessment and intervention planning.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 05: Bridging Minds and Machines: Mapping the Terrain of Communication in Human-AI Teams — A Systematic Literature Review (Wen Duan et al.)
item.description:
Bridging Minds and Machines: Mapping the Terrain of Communication in Human-AI Teams — A Systematic Literature Review - Wen Duan et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1145/3816906
Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction (2026). As AI becomes increasingly adept at communicating with humans in natural language and complementing human skills in various collaborative and teamwork settings, how the CSCW community understands the evolving role of communication in human-AI teams (HATs) urgently needs to keep pace with these technological advancements. To provide a structured overview of the scientific knowledge regarding communication in HATs, we conducted a systematic review of 74 articles, synthesizing how communication has been conceptualized, operationalized, and linked to team processes and outcomes. Our review reveals that existing research overwhelmingly relies on text-based communication and is concentrated in controlled experimental and simulated settings, with communication outcomes often measured using platform-specific or frequency-based metrics, limiting generalizability across tasks and contexts. Across this literature, communication is most commonly modeled through a functional input-output lens, leaving the communicative processes that transform inputs into taskwork and teamwork outcomes under-explored. We synthesize these findings into an input–process–output framework that reconceptualizes communication as a socially embedded team process, which can inform methodological choices and the purposeful and responsible design of communicative AI teammates in CSCW contexts.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 06: Sleep disorders and male sexual dysfunction: a meta-analysis of hormonal and erectile outcomes (Muath Almurayyi et al.)
item.description:
Sleep disorders and male sexual dysfunction: a meta-analysis of hormonal and erectile outcomes - Muath Almurayyi et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.4081/aiua.2026.15659
Archivio Italiano di Urologia e Andrologia (2026). BACKGROUND: Sleep disruptions, including insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), are strongly linked to male sexual dysfunction, affecting libido, erectile function, and hormonal balance. This metaanalysis aimed to evaluate the relationship between sleep disorders and male sexual function. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect through September 2025 identified 9 peer-reviewed studies examining the impact of sleep disorders on male sexual health. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used to assess the risk of bias. A meta-analysis was performed to evaluate outcomes, including the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF), testosterone, follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), and luteinizing hormone (LH) levels, with a subgroup analysis comparing OSA and shift work sleep disorder (SWSD). Statistical analyses were conducted using R version 4.2.2. RESULTS: Across seven studies (n = 913), the pooled mean IIEF score was approximately 16, indicating moderate erectile dysfunction, though heterogeneity was high (I² = 97.3%). Subgroup analysis revealed lower IIEF scores in OSA patients (≈14.4) compared to SWSD patients (≈17.5), suggesting more severe dysfunction in OSA. Hormonal analysis (n = 325) showed significantly lower testosterone levels in OSA (≈7-9 nmol/L) versus SWSD (≈20 nmol/L). FSH and LH were elevated in OSA (≈3.8-5.8 IU/L and 3.3-3.9 IU/L, respectively) compared to SWSD (≈2.2 IU/L and 1.8 IU/L). High heterogeneity indicated substantial variation in study design and populations. CONCLUSIONS: Both OSA and SWSD impair sexual and hormonal function, but OSA causes greater erectile and endocrine disruption. Even mild OSA was associated with reduced erectile performance, with the severity worsening dysfunction. Despite consistent trends, high heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation. Future research should employ standardized tools and uniform populations to clarify mechanisms linking sleep disorders to male sexual health.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - 07: A systematic review of delay discounting among workers: framing effects, resource availability, and health (Gisel G. Escobar et al.)
item.description:
A systematic review of delay discounting among workers: framing effects, resource availability, and health - Gisel G. Escobar et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1801136
Frontiers in Psychology (2026). A higher rate of delay discounting has been linked to a range of health-risk behaviors and adverse health outcomes. Despite its relevance, delay discounting has limited application in organizational contexts. The aim of this systematic review was to identify empirical studies on the application of delay discounting in organizations or among workers. Sixteen studies were included. Overall, contextual factors (resource availability and negative income shock) and methodological factors (framework, reward magnitude, task type) influenced delay discounting. Consistent effects were observed, including preference reversals, magnitude and sign effects, and clear distinctions between delay and probability discounting. Limitations include insufficient characterization of organizational variables, insufficient information on data systematicity and fit level of the mathematical discounting functions. Despite these limitations, delay discounting proved to be a sensitive and applicable behavioral indicator of increased self-control, capable of predicting adherence to a physical activity intervention in sedentary workers. The review also identifies opportunities for future research, including multidimensional delay discounting analysis, inter-outcome tasks, and the integration of comparison groups in health-related studies. Overall, delay discounting provides a practical framework for studying decision-making in organizational contexts and for guiding interventions to improve workers' self-regulation and long-term goal achievement.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - Spotlight: More than just smiling: how positive emotions are expressed on the face (Kunalan Manokara et al.)
item.description:
More than just smiling: how positive emotions are expressed on the face - Kunalan Manokara et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1098/rstb.2025.0133
Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences (2026). To advance the science of positive emotional expressions, we test how 22 positive emotions are spontaneously displayed on the face, using the participant-negotiated episodic recall method. Respondents (n = 163) narrated emotional events from their lives, and we extracted facial behaviours that reflected peak expressivity (35 410 facial actions). Network models were applied to probe whether specific positive emotions would be conditionally associated with particular facial behaviours. Our results point to three sets of positive emotions: five that do not seem to have specific facial actions related to them (e.g. admiration), nine whose expressions do not significantly involve smiling (e.g. head turn for interest, raised chin for determination), and eight whose facial expressions include smiling as a unique expressive feature (e.g. positive surprise and elation). Notably, nine of these positive emotions had expressive patterns that were distinct from the other emotions in our set (e.g. raised cheeks and closed eyes for sexual desire), while eight emotions were associated with expressive patterns that were shared in pairs (e.g. raised eyebrows for both hope and inspiration). These results provide a tentative map of what specific positive emotions look like when produced on the face in a naturalistic situation. This article is part of the theme issue 'Mechanisms, development, phylogeny and functions of emotional expressions'.

item.title: Oct W2 26 - Spotlight: The Impact of Sexual Satisfaction on Marital Adjustment, Quality of Life, and Treatment Adherence in Patients Diagnosed With Bipolar Disorder and Their Spouses: A Cross‐Sectional Study (Zerrin Demirel et al.)
item.description:
The Impact of Sexual Satisfaction on Marital Adjustment, Quality of Life, and Treatment Adherence in Patients Diagnosed With Bipolar Disorder and Their Spouses: A Cross‐Sectional Study - Zerrin Demirel et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1111/bdi.70189
Bipolar Disorders (2026). OBJECTIVES: To examine the effects of sexual satisfaction on marital adjustment, quality of life, and treatment adherence in patients diagnosed with bipolar disorder (BD) and their spouses. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 124 euthymic patients with BD and their spouses (124 couples; n = 248 individuals), recruited from the psychiatry outpatient clinics of Gaziantep University Şahinbey Research and Practice Hospital, Türkiye. Data were collected using a Sociodemographic Form, the Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS), the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), the Golombok-Rust Inventory of Sexual Satisfaction (GRISS), the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS), the Quality of Life in Bipolar Disorder Scale (QoL.BD), and the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS). RESULTS: Patients' mean age was 43.62 ± 9.68 years; 51.61% had been married for ≥ 21 years. Mean scores: BDI 6.6 ± 7.51, QoL.BD 43.93 ± 12.08, DAS 17.16 ± 6.36, GRISS 39.63 ± 23.72, MMAS 1.31 ± 1.35. Greater sexual dissatisfaction was associated with poorer marital adjustment (r = 0.325, p < 0.001). No significant direct association was found between sexual satisfaction and adherence. Higher quality of life was associated with lower depression, better marital adjustment, and greater sexual satisfaction. CONCLUSIONS: Sexual satisfaction is closely linked to marital adjustment and quality of life in BD, with a less direct relationship to treatment adherence. Couple-based psychoeducation addressing sexual health may support marital and quality-of-life outcomes in this population.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - 01: Modeling the rhythmic complexity of professional drumming with an oscillation-driven reservoir computer (Yuji Kawai et al.)
item.description:
Modeling the rhythmic complexity of professional drumming with an oscillation-driven reservoir computer - Yuji Kawai et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1007/s11571-026-10512-5
Cognitive Neurodynamics (2026). Musical performances, particularly in drumming, are characterized not only by their structured rhythmic patterns but also by the subtle variations in timing and amplitude series that create expressive complexity. This study proposes a neural-inspired computational model to investigate how the brain might learn and internalize such complex rhythms. Inspired by the established roles of the cerebellum and basal ganglia in production of rhythms and timings, we utilize an oscillation-driven reservoir computer, a recurrent neural network model for temporal learning, to simulate the generation of human-like expressive drumming performances. First, the model was trained to replicate Jeff Porcaro's distinctive hi-hat patterns. Analyses revealed that the outputs of the model incorporating high-frequency oscillators ([50, 100] Hz), closely matched the original drumming, reproducing its characteristic fluctuations and patterns in inter-beat timings (microtiming) and amplitudes. Next, the model was trained to generate multidimensional drum kit performances for various genres (funk, jazz, samba, and rock). The model's outputs exhibited timing deviation and audio features characteristic of the original performances. Our findings demonstrate that oscillation-driven reservoir computing can replicate the rhythmic complexity of professional drumming, suggesting it as a potential computational principle for motor timing and rhythm generation. This approach provides a powerful framework for understanding how the brain generates and processes intricate rhythmic patterns. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s11571-026-10512-5.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - 02: Drum Communication: Importance of Drum/Drumbeats in the Opu Ekine Sekiapu Dance of Nembe, Bayelsa State, Nigeria (Ikaderinyo Ibambo Furomfagha)
item.description:
Drum Communication: Importance of Drum/Drumbeats in the Opu Ekine Sekiapu Dance of Nembe, Bayelsa State, Nigeria - Ikaderinyo Ibambo Furomfagha - 2026 https://doi.org/10.52589/bjmcmr-a4ri1pe0
British Journal of Mass Communication and Media Research (2026). The Opu Ekine Sekiapu dance is a traditional art form that is deeply embedded in the cultural and social identity of the Nembe people. This dance features intricate and rhythmic drumming, which plays a vital role in the overall performance. The objective of the study is to explore the significance of drums and drumbeats in the Opu Ekine Sekiapu dance of Nembe, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. The study adopted the Syncopation: Unifying Musical Theory and Perceptionand the embedded cognition theory. The study uses a purposive non-probability sampling technique and employs a mixed-methodapproach, and utilizes a survey with a questionnaire and focus group discussions as data collection instruments. The findings reveal that in the Opu Ekine Sekiapu dance, the drum serves primarily as a communication tool. The drumbeat plays a critical role by determining pace, dance steps, and rhythm for the dancers' movements and performances. The study thus highlights the essential role of drums and drumbeats in the Opu Ekine Sekiapu dance of Nembe, Bayelsa State, Nigeria. It deepens our understanding of the cultural heritage and significance of this traditional dance form.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - 03: The Role of Positive Body Image in Eating Disorders: Invited Narrative Review on the Current Evidence, Therapeutic Potential, and Directions for Future Research (Jake Linardon et al.)
item.description:
The Role of Positive Body Image in Eating Disorders: Invited Narrative Review on the Current Evidence, Therapeutic Potential, and Directions for Future Research - Jake Linardon et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1002/eat.70229
International Journal of Eating Disorders (2026). OBJECTIVE: Stagnant improvements in eating disorder recovery rates have prompted calls for novel strategies to augment existing treatments. Fostering positive body image has emerged as one potentially promising avenue for treatment augmentation. In this narrative review, we evaluate this possibility by critically appraising research examining the role of positive body image in eating disorder psychopathology, with the aim of clarifying its therapeutic potential and guiding the next generation of research in this field. METHOD: We critically synthesized nearly two decades of research exploring the relevance of positive body image in eating disorders. RESULTS: A synthesis of empirical research provides evidence for the protective potential of positive body image: prospective studies suggest that body appreciation, functionality appreciation, and body image flexibility are associated with reduced eating disorder symptoms, while intervention research indicates that these components are amenable to change and may contribute to symptom improvement during eating disorder treatment. CONCLUSION: The current evidence provides a solid foundation for recognizing the clinical potential of fostering positive body image in eating disorder treatment, while also highlighting uncertainty about how, when, and for whom it may be most beneficial. We provide a series of future directions necessary for more fully understanding the clinical importance of positive body image in eating disorders and guiding its future integration into treatment.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - 04: How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis (Jingwen Li et al.)
item.description:
How School-Based Interventions Shape the Developing Brain during 3-12 Years: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis - Jingwen Li et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dcn.2026.101831
Developmental Cognitive Neuroscience (2026). The effects of school-based interventions (SBIs) on children’s neurodevelopment are poorly synthesized. This systematic review integrates neuroscientific evidence on how structured educational activities influence brain development in children aged 3-12 years. Following PRISMA guidelines, we identified 17 empirical studies (published 2014–2025) using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), electroencephalography (EEG), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). Of these, 8 studies were included in a random-effects meta-analysis and all 17 in a thematic synthesis. The meta-analysis revealed a preliminary association between SBIs and reduced amygdala activity during stress regulation tasks ( r = –.28, 95% CI [–.50, –.02]), based on two studies, which should be interpreted as exploratory rather than confirmatory. No significant pooled effect for executive function, likely due to high heterogeneity. Thematic analysis distinguishes between mechanisms of plasticity and markers of intervention effectiveness: the first three characterize intra-individual mechanisms of experience-dependent plasticity, including (1) executive function interventions engaged prefrontal networks through both increased recruitment and enhanced neural efficiency; (2) socio-emotional programs modulated limbic-prefrontal circuits; (3) language and auditory programs shaped sensory-specific electrophysiological markers and cortical specialization; and the fourth theme identifies a neural marker of the effective process of intervention delivery, demonstrating that (4) teacher-child inter-brain synchrony was positively correlated with learning outcomes. By integrating findings across neural, cognitive, and affective domains, this review provides a conceptual framework linking pedagogical practices to neural plasticity and advances the understanding of the neurofunctional pathways through which educational experiences shape the developing brain.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - 05: CHUNK-BASED COMMUNICATIVE LANGUAGE TEACHING AND ITS IMPACT ON INDONESIAN EFL STUDENTS’ SPEAKING FLUENCY: A NARRATIVE REVIEW (Muhammad Pandu Khoiron et al.)
item.description:
CHUNK-BASED COMMUNICATIVE LANGUAGE TEACHING AND ITS IMPACT ON INDONESIAN EFL STUDENTS’ SPEAKING FLUENCY: A NARRATIVE REVIEW - Muhammad Pandu Khoiron et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.31943/wej.v10i2.744
Wiralodra English Journal (2026). The current narrative literature review aimed to investigate the use of Chunk-Based CLT as a pedagogical technique to enhance the fluency of EFL students from Indonesia. Even though the students have been receiving formal English education in all stages from primary to tertiary levels, many still experience difficulties in their fluency due to the high cognitive load and their tendency to translate from word to word. In order to explore this problem, the literature synthesis was performed using academic works related to formulaic language and communicative pedagogy. It turned out that lexical chunks (prefabricated formulaic sequences) help learners acquire important cognitive shortcuts and minimize unnatural pausing, increase speech rate and reduce the anxiety about making grammatical mistakes during language learning in a foreign language. Besides, engaging the learners with these linguistic units in communicative activities is beneficial for producing natural speech. Thus, the pedagogical relevance of this method of instruction in EFL context is highly significant. Based on the findings made, this paper shows that the chunk-based instruction is useful in bridging the fluency gap. To continue this research, further empirical studies need to be performed experimentally.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - 06: Sexual Dysregulation After Traumatic Brain Injury and Stroke: A Critical Narrative Review of Neurobiology, Clinical Phenotypes, and Management (Rocco Salvatore Calabrò et al.)
item.description:
Sexual Dysregulation After Traumatic Brain Injury and Stroke: A Critical Narrative Review of Neurobiology, Clinical Phenotypes, and Management - Rocco Salvatore Calabrò et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.3390/brainsci16090995
Brain Sciences (2026). Background/Objectives: Acquired brain injury (ABI) can disturb sexual regulation, but the literature does not support a single lesion-to-behavior relationship. This critical narrative review evaluates hypersexuality, sexual disinhibition, and rare acquired paraphilic manifestations after traumatic brain injury (TBI) and stroke, and asks how sparse, heterogeneous evidence can inform proportionate clinical care. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to 6 August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and full texts. Evidence appraisal considered methodological quality, directness, and competing explanations. Thirteen English-language case-based publications were assessed, with neurological observations distinguished from pharmacological comparators. Results: Sexual dysfunction is common after ABI, whereas dysregulated sexual behavior is less frequent and poorly quantified. TBI primarily supports a distributed vulnerability model involving diffuse axonal injury and disruption of frontal regulatory connections. Stroke can nominate strategic candidate nodes, but lesion-network effects and clinical context remain decisive. Clinical observations associate inappropriate sexual behavior with broader behavioral difficulties, without establishing a uniform syndrome. Recent guidelines support individualized sexuality care, while contemporary imaging studies strengthen network plausibility without directly establishing sexual-dysregulation mechanisms. Conclusions: A phenotype-first framework separates dysfunction from dysregulation and distinguishes direct clinical evidence from mechanistic extrapolation. Assessment should establish what changed and whether reversible contributors explain the behavior before assigning a persistent phenotype. Management should match the dominant clinical problem, preserve consensual intimacy, and use the least restrictive targeted strategy. Explicit monitoring should determine whether benefit justifies continued treatment. Case-based evidence and language-restricted selection limit generalizability; prospective studies require standardized phenotypes and repeated observation across settings.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - 07: Clarifying Online Cooperative Learning in EFL Contexts: A Systematic Review of Learning Outcomes, the Five Core Elements, and Implementation Challenges (Zhang Aijia et al.)
item.description:
Clarifying Online Cooperative Learning in EFL Contexts: A Systematic Review of Learning Outcomes, the Five Core Elements, and Implementation Challenges - Zhang Aijia et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.26803/ijlter.25.8.18
International Journal of Learning Teaching and Educational Research (2026). Although online cooperative learning has been widely examined in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) education, it is often conceptually blurred with less structured forms of collaborative learning. This review synthesised empirical articles on online cooperative learning in EFL contexts, focusing on study characteristics, reported outcomes, the operationalisation of Johnson and Johnson’s five elements, and implementation challenges. PRISMA 2020, Eric, Web of Science, Scopus, and ProQuest were searched for empirical English-language journal articles published up to June 2026. Twenty-five studies met the eligibility criteria and were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Mixed-methods designs were the most common (56%, n = 14), university settings dominated the studies (80%, n = 20), and writing was the leading focus (40%, n = 10). Of the 17 studies using inferential tests of language-related performance, 16 reported statistically significant positive gains or associations, although the strength of evidence varied. Positive interdependence was explicitly reported in 20 studies and implied in 5. In contrast, small-group skills and group processing were explicitly reported in only[1] 3 and 7 studies, respectively. The main implementation challenges involved weak technological–pedagogical alignment, insufficient instructional scaffolding, and uneven participation and accountability. The findings suggest that online cooperative learning should be conceptualized not according to named cooperative structures alone, but according to how the online cooperative EFL learning environment, instructional configuration, and the five core cooperative learning elements are integrated. Future research should design clearly structured online cooperative EFL courses across more diverse educational settings, language areas, and learner groups, particularly for learners with lower language proficiency or limited digital literacy.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - Spotlight: Rasa, Bhav and Abhinaya : A pathway to ‘Meditation in Motion’ (Radhika Gowardhan)
item.description:
Rasa, Bhav and Abhinaya : A pathway to ‘Meditation in Motion’ - Radhika Gowardhan - 2026 https://doi.org/10.67754/ijiis.special.edi2.vol02.0016
Abhinavdhara International Journal of Innovation in Indic Studies (2026). Dance is one of the earliest and most fundamental modes of human expression, emerging alongside the evolution of humanity as a means of communicating emotion through bhava and expression through rasa and abhinaya.From spontaneous movement to structured forms, dance has developed across countries in different forms and is part of human rituals, celebration and festivals.Rasa -The Sanskrit word for 'essence' can directly lead to a meditative state; by engaging deeply with the present moment through emotions, art, or sensory experiences, rasa serves as an entry point to calm the mind and enter a meditative state.Bhava -The Sanskrit word for feeling can naturally lead to meditation.By directing and channelising one's emotional energies by focussing on mind and transitions your awareness into a state of deep one-pointed concentration.Abhinaya -The art of dramatic expression and acting) can be a profound pathway to meditation both practices require intense present moment awareness breath control and the ability to detach from the ego to fully embody a subject.Thus, a combination of the three pillars of dancing rsa, bhava and abhinaya leads to a complete meditative state of the mind where there is a performer is only in the present and is without self-awareness and ego and had become one with character and the performance just flows though just like soft wind touches the nostril whole breathing.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - Spotlight: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Addressing Chronic Cancer Pain: A Narrative Review with Considerations for Utilization in Primary Care (Nina Hanenson Russin et al.)
item.description:
Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Addressing Chronic Cancer Pain: A Narrative Review with Considerations for Utilization in Primary Care - Nina Hanenson Russin et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare14193232
Healthcare (2026). Background: Chronic pain is common among cancer survivors and may reflect interacting physical, psychological, social, and existential factors. Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a behavioral intervention that emphasizes psychological flexibility, acceptance, present-moment awareness, and values-guided action. As cancer survivorship care increasingly involves primary care, scalable behavioral approaches may be needed to complement medical pain management, particularly where specialty behavioral health resources are limited. Methods: This narrative review examined evidence for ACT in chronic cancer-related pain and its potential applicability to primary care and resource-constrained healthcare settings. Searches were conducted in PubMed, PsycINFO, and CINAHL Ultimate, supplemented by Google Scholar and the Association for Contextual Behavioral Science database. Fifteen studies met criteria for inclusion. Results: ACT showed promising effects on outcomes including psychological flexibility, pain acceptance, emotional distress, quality of life, pain coping, and pain-related functioning, whereas findings for pain intensity were less consistent. The evidence was limited by heterogeneous study designs and populations and generally small experimental samples. None of the included studies directly evaluated ACT for cancer-related pain in primary care, although studies in other chronic pain and mental health populations provide indirect support for the feasibility of ACT in primary care and community settings. Discussion: Although direct evidence for the utilization of ACT in primary care is lacking, studies on ACT interventions for chronic pain and mental illness in these settings suggest that brief ACT interventions for cancer pain may help to address the need for behavioral health support. Future research should include pragmatic trials to determine whether brief ACT-informed interventions can be feasibly integrated into multidisciplinary primary care teams and delivered through digital or hybrid models.

item.title: Oct W1 26 - Spotlight: Associations between muscle dysmorphia symptoms and sexual functioning among sexually active boys and young men (Kyle T. Ganson et al.)
item.description:
Associations between muscle dysmorphia symptoms and sexual functioning among sexually active boys and young men - Kyle T. Ganson et al. - 2026 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bodyim.2026.102201
Body Image (2026). Muscle dysmorphia is characterized by a pathological pursuit of muscularity, pronounced body dissatisfaction, and functional impairment. Although muscle dysmorphia symptoms have been linked with numerous adverse health and psychosocial correlates, its association with sexual functioning among boys and young men remains underexplored. This study examined associations between muscle dysmorphia symptoms and sexual dysfunction among sexually active boys and men (N = 1116). Data were drawn from The Study of Boys and Men, an online survey of males aged 15-35 years recruited via social media advertisements in 2024. Muscle dysmorphia symptoms were assessed using the Muscle Dysmorphic Disorder Inventory (MDDI), and eight domains of sexual functioning (e.g., anxiety, lack of arousal, physical pain, erectile dysfunction) were assessed using items from the National Survey of Sexual Attitudes and Lifestyles Sexual Functioning measure. Multiple logistic and linear regression models tested associations between MDDI scores (Drive for Size, Appearance Intolerance, Functional Impairment, and total score) and eight forms of sexual dysfunction, as well as an aggregate count of sexual dysfunction, adjusting for sociodemographic covariates. Greater muscle dysmorphia symptoms, particularly Appearance Intolerance and the MDDI total score, were consistently associated with a broad range of sexual dysfunction and a greater number of sexual dysfunctions. Drive for Size and Functional Impairment showed fewer, smaller, significant associations. These findings suggest that sexual dysfunction may co-occur with muscle dysmorphia among sexually active boys and young men, underscoring the importance of assessing and addressing sexual health within clinical and preventive interventions targeting boys' and men's body image.
